title: Section C J4 (API leg): every alert text, including the deployer-chosen token symbol, is broadcast to the dashboard unmodified, and the notification severity and category are guessed from keywords in that text, so a token named for example "FAILED" or "SOLD" changes how the operator's event feed colours and files the alert

evidence.note: symbol and name are read from the token contract (deployer-controlled)
the New Token alert embeds the symbol raw
inferSeverity / inferCategory: substring matches on the whole message ('fail' -> error, 'sold' -> success, 'risk' -> warning, ...)
sendCtxAlert broadcasts { severity: inferSeverity(message), message, category: inferCategory(message) }
broadcast forwards the JSON to every client with no length cap or sanitising
rendered as React text ({evt.message}), so no HTML injection

sibling_sites_checked: Every broadcast() caller at the base SHA (git grep "broadcast(" -- src): notifier.ts:54 and :91 carry free text; circuitBreaker.ts, detector.ts, exitTrigger.ts, chains.ts, controls.ts and server.ts send structured fields (addresses, numbers, enums). The Telegram Markdown injection of the same symbol is AUD-BUY-022 (BUY slice, SC-10), the canonical entry for the unescaped symbol; this entry is the dashboard-transport and severity-guessing leg owned by the API slice. Dashboard rendering of the text (React escaping) is audited in the DASH slice.
severity_rationale: S3: misleading operator display only; the text is escaped when rendered and nothing in the bot acts on the guessed severity.
recommendation: Send severity and category as explicit fields from each alert site instead of guessing from the text, and clip and sanitise token-controlled strings at the source (sanitize.ts already exists). Phase 29.
